header.userPrompt:
Speed up the server test suite by using a SINGLE shared Postgres container for the entire test run,
instead of today's per-test container. Server TEST code only — do NOT change production code.

PROBLEM: `server/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/core/PostgresSpec.scala` extends
`com.dimafeng.testcontainers.scalatest.TestContainerForEach`, so EVERY test starts a fresh `postgres:13`
container, runs `CREATE EXTENSION CITEXT`, and `Evolutions.applyEvolutions(...)`, then tears it down.
With ~67 specs this is hundreds of serialized container start/evolve/stop cycles and dominates the suite
(and CI) runtime.

GOAL: one Postgres container started ONCE for the whole test JVM and shared by ALL server specs, with
evolutions applied ONCE against it. Because the DB is now shared and NOT reset between tests, tests must
isolate themselves with RANDOM, user-scoped data rather than relying on a pristine/empty DB.

BUILD:
1. Shared singleton container:
   - Introduce a single long-lived `postgres:13` container started once per test JVM (e.g. a lazy
     `object SharedPostgres`), with `CREATE EXTENSION CITEXT` and `Evolutions.applyEvolutions` run exactly
     once against it (guard so repeated access does not re-run them). Do NOT stop it per test/suite — let
     it live for the JVM (Ryuk / a shutdown hook cleans it up).
   - Rework `PostgresSpec` so `withDatabase` returns the shared `Database` (no per-test container). Keep the
     same `withDatabase[T](runTest: Database => T): T` signature so repository specs need no call-site
     change beyond data isolation.
   - Rework the controller/Play base the same way: the `guiceApplicationBuilder(container)` specs must build
     their Play app against the SHARED container's JDBC url (point the DB config at the singleton), not a
     per-test container. Evolutions are already applied to the shared DB; Play's startup evolutions must not
     fight that (they are idempotent once applied).
2. Test isolation via random data (the behavioral change):
   - Add a small test helper for unique random values (e.g. `randomEmail()`, `randomName()`, random strings)
     and use it wherever a test inserts rows with UNIQUE columns (emails, names, etc.). Entity ids are
     already UUIDv7 (unique) — keep using fresh ids per test.
   - Every test must create and assert on ITS OWN data, scoped to its own user. Remove assumptions that the
     DB is empty or globally small: no "the table has exactly N rows", no "list returns all X across the
     whole DB", no asserting on global counts. Scope list/count assertions to the test's own user or the
     specific rows it created (presence/shape, not global totals).
3. Fix the fallout, not every spec blindly:
   - Implement the shared container, run the full server suite, and FIX the specs that now fail under
     sharing — collisions on unique columns (switch to random values) and global-state assertions (scope
     them). Specs that are already user-scoped and use fresh ids may need no change. Do not weaken an
     assertion beyond scoping it to the test's own data.

CONSTRAINTS:
- Server TEST sources only (`server/src/test`). No production code change. No new DB evolution. No
  dependency changes (testcontainers is already present); revert incidental yarn.lock churn.
- Keep `Test / fork := true` for server. Do NOT enable cross-run container reuse (`withReuse` /
  testcontainers.reuse) — that is for local dev and risks stale state in CI. This change is a single
  container per RUN, not persisted across runs.
- Do NOT change test parallelism settings in this PR (correctness of the shared-container + random-data
  model first; parallelism can be a follow-up).
- Follow docs/guide/testing.md. Attribution: NO Claude session links in commits or the PR description;
  `Co-Authored-By: Claude` IS allowed.

VERIFY:
- The full server suite passes with a single shared container: confirm (via logs) that the container is
  started once, not per test. Targeted `sbt "testOnly *Spec"` while iterating; the final stage runs the
  whole suite (`CI=true NODE_OPTIONS=--openssl-legacy-provider sbt test`).
- Do not regress coverage — the same specs run, only their data setup/isolation changes.

resultJson.description:
Server tests currently start a fresh `postgres:13` testcontainer for every test case. `PostgresSpec` (repository/action specs) and `PlayPostgresSpec` (controller specs, `GuiceOneServerPerTest`) both mix in `TestContainerForEach`, and each test runs `CREATE EXTENSION CITEXT` plus `Evolutions.applyEvolutions`. With about 40 DB-backed specs and hundreds of test cases, these serial start/evolve/stop cycles account for most of the server suite and CI runtime. This epic replaces them with one lazily started Postgres container per test JVM (`SharedPostgres`). CITEXT and the evolutions run on it exactly once, and every DB-backed spec uses it. The public test API stays the same: `withDatabase[T](runTest: Database => T): T` and `guiceApplicationBuilder(container: PostgreSQLContainer)`. That way the 15 controller-spec overrides and all repository call sites keep compiling.

Because the DB is no longer reset between tests, each test must isolate itself. It creates its own users with random emails and its own rows with random values in every UNIQUE column: user email, telegram_user_id, telegram link token, mcp token_hash, textract_cache (sha256, api_type), and so on. Its assertions cover only that data. Assertions on global state, like `users.all()` length, "no users" or `claimJobs(...).length must be(1)`, are scoped to the test's own rows. The background_jobs table is a global queue with no user_id and no foreign keys, and `claimJobs` is global by type. So the two claim-semantics specs explicitly clear that queue at the start of each test. This is safe because suites run sequentially in one forked JVM.

The isolation work comes first and is valid under the current per-test containers, so every task leaves the suite green. The container switch comes after it, and the DocumentsS3IntegrationSpec migration comes last. Scope: `server/src/test` only. No production code, evolutions, dependency, `Test / fork` or parallelism changes. No `withReuse`. Revert any incidental yarn.lock churn.

tasks.title: Add a RandomData test helper and make the RepositoryUtils factory defaults collision-free
tasks.description: Create `server/src/test/scala/utils/RandomData.scala` (an `object RandomData`) with small helpers: `randomString(prefix: String = "t"): String` (prefix + UUID without dashes), `randomEmail(): Email` (`Email.trusted(s"test-${UUID.randomUUID()}@wiringbits.net")`), `randomName(): Name`, `randomTelegramUserId(): Long` (positive, e.g. `ThreadLocalRandom.current().nextLong(1L, Long.MaxValue)`) and `randomTokenHash(): String` (64 lowercase hex chars). Change `RepositoryUtils.createUser` so its `email` default is `randomEmail()` instead of the fixed `hello@wiringbits.net`. Also look at the other defaults in `RepositoryUtils` that end up in UNIQUE columns. `createDocument`'s `sha256 = "abc123"` is only unique per user, so leave it unless a spec relies on it. Change a default only if the same user could call it twice by accident, and grep the callers first, because some specs rely on duplicate-sha behaviour on purpose. `LoginUtils.createUser` already randomizes its email; leave it. Verify: `CI=true sbt Test/compile`, then `sbt "server/testOnly *UsersRepositorySpec *CategoriesRepositorySpec"`. Both still use per-test containers and must stay green.

tasks.title: Isolate repository and action specs with random unique values and user-scoped assertions
tasks.description:
Go through `server/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/repositories/*Spec.scala` (except BackgroundJobsRepositorySpec, which is a separate task) and `net/wiringbits/actions/**` DB specs (`TelegramExpenseActionSpec`, `TelegramPhotoActionSpec`, `ResolveStatementSuggestionsActionSpec`). Replace hardcoded values in globally UNIQUE columns with `RandomData` values:
- the `Email.trusted("a@test.com")`/`"b@test.com"`/`"u1@test.com"`/`"u2@test.com"` pairs in the Expenses, Refunds, Merchants, BankStatement, Savings, Categories, Documents, Receipt and ImportRule repository specs. Usually just call `createUser()`, which now has a random default.
- `UsersRepositorySpec`: `email2@wiringbits.net`, the `test$i@wiringbits.net` loop, and the "doesn't exist" lookup of `hello@wiringbits.net`, which must use a random never-inserted email.
- `TelegramRepositorySpec`: link tokens (`abc123`, `duptoken1`, `findme01`, `todelete1`) and telegram user ids (100L/200L/300L/400L/999L). Use the same random value twice inside a test when the test asserts a duplicate failure.
- the `fakeTelegramUserId` constants in the Telegram action specs.
- `McpRepositorySpec` token hashes (`"b" * 64`, `"c" * 64`).
- the `DocumentsRepositorySpec` textract_cache keys (`"mysha256"`, `"global"`).

Scope global assertions in `UsersRepositorySpec`:
- `all` "return the existing users": assert that the 3 created ids/emails are all in `all()`, not `length must be(3)`.
- "return no users": cannot hold on a shared DB. Rewrite it as a scoped check, e.g. `all()` does not contain a random never-created id, and keep the test name descriptive.
- the three "produce a notification for the user" tests: stop calling global `claimJobs(...).length must be(1)`. Add a private helper that selects background_jobs rows whose JSONB payload email equals the test user's email, e.g. `payload->>'email' = {email}`, parsed with `net.wiringbits.repositories.daos.backgroundJobParser`. Assert exactly one SendEmail job exists for that user.

Also check `BugFixSpec`, `TextractJobRepositorySpec`, `TelegramReceiptRepositorySpec`, `UserTokensRepositorySpec` and `UserLogsRepositorySpec` for fixed unique values or whole-table assertions. Most are already scoped by user id and need no change. Do not weaken any assertion beyond scoping it to the test's own rows. Verify with targeted `sbt "server/testOnly net.wiringbits.repositories.* net.wiringbits.actions.*"` (still per-test containers) and `CI=true sbt Test/compile`.

tasks.title: Make background-job queue specs independent of jobs left behind by other specs
tasks.description: `BackgroundJobsRepository.claimJobs(jobType, timeout, limit)` and `BackgroundJobTypeRunner.source` claim jobs globally by type, ordered by execute_at. Once the DB is shared, pending SendEmail/ProcessDocument jobs left by other specs would be claimed too. This breaks assertions such as `result.map(_.id) must be(List(createRequest.id))`, `result must be(empty)`, `started.get() must be(5)` and the error-limit test in `BackgroundJobTypeRunnerSpec`, which uses a clock 2 days ahead. background_jobs has no user_id and no inbound foreign keys, and suites run sequentially in one forked JVM. Because of that, add a helper to `utils/RepositoryUtils`, e.g. `def clearBackgroundJobs()(using repositories: RepositoryComponents): Unit`, which runs `DELETE FROM background_jobs` via `repositories.database.withConnection`. Add a ScalaDoc comment explaining that background_jobs is a global, non-user-scoped queue and that claim semantics can only be tested against an empty queue. Call it at the start of every test in `server/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/repositories/BackgroundJobsRepositorySpec.scala` and `server/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/tasks/BackgroundJobTypeRunnerSpec.scala`. A clean way is a spec-local wrapper around `withRepositories()` that clears first, which avoids touching every test body. Keep every existing assertion unchanged. Do not use this helper anywhere else; other specs scope by user. Verify: `sbt "server/testOnly *BackgroundJobsRepositorySpec *BackgroundJobTypeRunnerSpec"`.

tasks.title: Isolate controller specs with random emails and telegram ids
tasks.description:
In `server/src/test/scala/controllers/*Spec.scala`, replace hardcoded unique values with `RandomData` values.
- `UsersControllerSpec`: about 15 uses of `test1@email.com`, `test@email.com` and `test@wiringbits.net`. Each test should create its own email via `randomEmail()` and reuse it within that test. Negative tests such as "ignore the request ... nonexistent email" and "fail when user's email is not registered" must use a fresh random email that was never registered.
- `AuthControllerSpec`: 3 fixed emails.
- `TelegramWebAppControllerSpec`: fixed `telegramUserId` values 54321L, 99999L and 77777L, plus any fixed emails.
- Grep the remaining controller specs (Expenses, Merchants, Refunds, Documents, Receipts, Savings, ImportRules, BankStatementDraft, Categories, Mcp, MerchantReview, BankStatements, EnvironmentConfig) for `Email.trusted("` and other fixed unique values. Also look for assertions that rely on a globally empty DB. Most go through user-scoped API calls after `createVerifyLoginUser` and need no change.

Keep Mockito-based token determinism as is. `tokenGenerator` UUIDs are already random per test. Do not change the `guiceApplicationBuilder(container: PostgreSQLContainer)` overrides. Verify with targeted runs such as `sbt "server/testOnly controllers.UsersControllerSpec controllers.AuthControllerSpec controllers.TelegramWebAppControllerSpec"`, plus `CI=true sbt Test/compile`.

tasks.title: Replace per-test containers with a single shared Postgres container for the test JVM
tasks.description:
Add `server/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/core/SharedPostgres.scala`: an `object SharedPostgres` whose lazy initialization (Scala 3 lazy vals are thread-safe) does the following:
- Starts one `PostgreSQLContainer.Def(dockerImageName = DockerImageName.parse("postgres:13")).start()`.
- Logs a single line via slf4j, e.g. `Started shared Postgres container at <jdbcUrl>`, so the final full run can confirm it started once.
- Runs `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS CITEXT` over a `DriverManager` connection.
- Builds `Databases(driver = "org.postgresql.Driver", url = jdbcUrl, name = "default", config = Map("username" -> ..., "password" -> ...))`.
- Runs `Evolutions.applyEvolutions(database)` once.
- Exposes `container: PostgreSQLContainer` and `database: Database`. Accessing `container` must also trigger the CITEXT and evolutions setup, e.g. one lazy val holding both. Do not stop it per suite. Ryuk cleans it up at JVM exit, optionally with a `sys.addShutdownHook` that shuts down the Database pool and stops the container. Never use `withReuse`.

Rewrite `net/wiringbits/core/PostgresSpec.scala`: drop `TestContainerForEach`, `containerDef` and `initDatabase`. Keep `trait PostgresSpec { self: Suite => def withDatabase[T](runTest: Database => T): T = runTest(SharedPostgres.database) }`.

Rewrite `controllers/common/PlayPostgresSpec.scala`: drop `TestContainerForEach` and `containerDef`. Keep `def guiceApplicationBuilder(container: PostgreSQLContainer): GuiceApplicationBuilder` with the same signature and config map, so all 15 overrides compile untouched. `newAppForTest` should become `guiceApplicationBuilder(SharedPostgres.container).build()` with no CITEXT step. Play's startup evolutions (`play.evolutions.autoApply = true` in application.conf) find play_evolutions already up to date and do nothing. Remove imports these changes leave unused, since `-Werror` is on with CI=true.

Then run the DB-backed specs with targeted runs: `sbt "server/testOnly net.wiringbits.repositories.* net.wiringbits.actions.* net.wiringbits.tasks.*"` and `sbt "server/testOnly controllers.*"`. Check the logs for a single startup line per JVM. Fix any remaining collisions or global-state assertions by scoping them to the test's own data, never by weakening them. Do not change fork or parallelism settings. Run `CI=true sbt Test/compile` and `sbt scalafmtAll`.

tasks.title: Move DocumentsS3IntegrationSpec's Postgres onto the shared container
tasks.description:
`server/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/actions/documents/DocumentsS3IntegrationSpec.scala` starts its own Postgres through `ForAllTestContainer` with `MultipleContainers(postgres, s3mock)`. It also applies CITEXT and evolutions itself, and its `cleanAll()` runs `DELETE FROM background_jobs / document / users`. On the shared DB that would delete other specs' data, and it fails on the users foreign keys. Changes:
- Keep `ForAllTestContainer`, but with only the `s3mock` GenericContainer: `override val container = s3mock`, or `MultipleContainers(s3mock)`.
- Make `db` use `SharedPostgres.database`. Remove the `beforeStop` `db.shutdown()`, since the shared pool must stay open.
- Change `cleanAll()` so it only empties the S3 bucket, with no DB deletes.
- Keep `makeUser()` and its random `test_${id}@example.com` email.

The tests are already user-scoped, e.g. `documentsRepo.all(userId)` and `find(id, userId)`, so the assertions stay as they are. Change the fixed sha256 `"orphansha"` only if it can collide, since it is unique per user and each test makes a fresh user. Remove the imports this change leaves unused. Verify with `sbt "server/testOnly *DocumentsS3IntegrationSpec"` and `CI=true sbt Test/compile`.

resultJson.brief:
Modules/dirs
- `server/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/core/`: `PostgresSpec` (DB base trait, currently `TestContainerForEach`), `RepositorySpec` (`AnyWordSpec with PostgresSpec`; `withRepositories[T](clock: Clock = Clock.systemUTC)(runTest: RepositoryComponents => T): T` builds every repository on top of `withDatabase`), `RepositoryComponents` (case class holding `database: Database` plus every repository).
- `server/src/test/scala/controllers/common/PlayPostgresSpec.scala`: `PlayAPISpec with TestContainerForEach with GuiceOneServerPerTest`. `newAppForTest` creates CITEXT, then `guiceApplicationBuilder(postgres).build()`. `def guiceApplicationBuilder(container: com.dimafeng.testcontainers.PostgreSQLContainer): GuiceApplicationBuilder` overrides `db.default.url/username/password` via `Configuration.from(map).withFallback(Configuration.load(env))`. 15 controller specs override it as `super.guiceApplicationBuilder(container).overrides(...)`, so keep that signature exactly. The trait also has `withApiClient`, `createBankStatementWithRows`, and `RichFutureExt.expectError`.
- `server/src/test/scala/utils/`: `RepositoryUtils` (trait with factories; `createUser(email: Email = Email.trusted("hello@wiringbits.net"))(using RepositoryComponents)(using ExecutionContext)` is the main collision source; `createBackgroundJobData(...)` inserts via `BackgroundJobDAO.create`), `LoginUtils` (API-level `createUser`/`createVerifyLoginUser(tokenGenerator, nameMaybe, emailMaybe, passwordMaybe)`; already defaults to a random `test${UUID}@email.com`), `Executors` (`globalEC`, `databaseEC`).
- `DocumentsS3IntegrationSpec` (own Postgres plus s3mock via `ForAllTestContainer`) and `S3BlobStorageSpec` (s3mock only) don't use PostgresSpec.

DB facts (`server/src/main/resources/evolutions/default/{1,2,3}.sql`)
- Globally UNIQUE: `users.email` (citext, case-insensitive), `telegram_link_token.token`, `telegram_bot_user.telegram_user_id`, `mcp_api_token.token_hash`, `mcp_api_token.user_id` (one token per user), `textract_cache (sha256, api_type)`, `receipt.document_id`, `bank_statement.document_id`, `telegram_receipt.receipt_id`.
- Unique per user only (safe once each test has its own user): category/merchant/savings_goal `(user_id, name)`, `document (user_id, sha256)`, `merchant_rule (user_id, pattern[, merchant_id])`, `merchant (user_id, tax_id)`.
- `background_jobs` (2.sql) has no user_id and no inbound FKs. `payload` is JSONB; `BackgroundJobPayload.SendEmail(email: Email, subject, body)` is serialized with play-json `Json.format`, so the email is at `payload->>'email'`. Check how `BackgroundJobDAO` stores `type`/`status` before filtering on them in SQL. Parser: `net.wiringbits.repositories.daos.backgroundJobParser`.
- `claimJobs(jobType, timeout: FiniteDuration, limit: Int)` is global by type, ordered by execute_at, and uses SKIP LOCKED. `UsersRepository` updatePassword/verify/resetPassword enqueue SendEmail jobs.

Play app facts
- application.conf has `play.evolutions.autoApply = true`. Once the shared DB is evolved, Play's startup check is a no-op. (The PlayPostgresSpec ScalaDoc claims evolutions are disabled, but they are not.)
- Every Play app starts `BackgroundJobsExecutorTask`, which first polls after `backgroundJobsExecutorTask.interval` (1 minute). Per-test apps normally stop before then, but leftover jobs from other specs could be dispatched in a test that runs longer than a minute. Keep this in mind if a controller test turns flaky.
- The controller specs use `GuiceOneServerPerTest`, so a new app and Hikari pool is created per test against the given JDBC URL.

Build/test conventions
- Scala 3 (`using`/`given`, `*` imports). `CI=true` enables `-Werror`, so remove unused imports. Format with `sbt scalafmtAll`.
- `build.sbt` server settings: `Test / fork := true` (line ~342) and testcontainers-scala 0.44.1 (`com.dimafeng.testcontainers.{PostgreSQLContainer, ForAllTestContainer, GenericContainer, MultipleContainers}`). Suites run sequentially in the forked JVM. Do NOT touch fork, parallelism or dependencies, and do not use `withReuse`/testcontainers.reuse.
- `PostgreSQLContainer.Def(dockerImageName = DockerImageName.parse("postgres:13")).start()` returns a started Scala wrapper exposing `jdbcUrl`, `username`, `password` and `.container` (the Java container).
- Test style (docs/guide/testing.md): ScalaTest `AnyWordSpec`/`PlaySpec`, `"method" should { "behaviour" in withRepositories() { implicit repositories => ... } }`, never repeat the class name in `should` subjects, `.futureValue` for futures, `.expectError` for expected failures, seed through `RepositoryUtils` factories rather than raw INSERTs. Raw SQL in tests is only for reads/inspection (e.g. `jobOf`) and the documented queue clear. Factories and `Email.trusted`/`Name.trusted` skip validation.
- Iterate with targeted `sbt "server/testOnly <pattern>"` or `CI=true sbt Test/compile`. Never run the full `sbt test` inside a task; a final stage does that.
- Scope is `server/src/test` only. docs/guide/testing.md RULE-TE-002 says "tears down after each test", which becomes stale, but docs are outside this PR's stated scope; note it in the PR rather than editing it.
- Commits: `Co-Authored-By: Claude` is allowed; no Claude session links.

Non-obvious gotchas
- Error-message assertions must keep matching the real constraint names, e.g. `users_email_unique`, `telegram_bot_user_telegram_user_id_unique`, `telegram_link_token_token_unique`. When testing duplicates, generate one random value and insert it twice in the same test.
- `users.all()` is global with no user filter, so assert containment of your own rows, never a length.
- `DocumentsS3IntegrationSpec.cleanAll()` does `DELETE FROM users`. That cannot run on the shared DB (FKs, and other specs' data).
- `createBankStatementWithRows` in PlayPostgresSpec schedules its ResolveStatementSuggestions job 365 days ahead on purpose, so the live executor never touches it. Keep that.
- Tests that toggle mocks (e.g. `captchaApi` returning false) reset them at the end. Preserve that pattern; mocks are shared per spec instance.

findings.title: Setting keys flagged as unused in build.sbt

reason.text: Out of scope and a false positive. This change only touches server/src/test, and the plan forbids editing build.sbt. These settings were already there before this branch. The scalajs-bundler and ScalablyTyped tasks (webpack, fastOptJS/fullOptJS, the dev server, stMinimize) read them, but lintUnused can't see that because this run only compiled. If the warning is worth silencing, a separate build-config change should add them to excludeLintKeys.

findings.title: Unused build settings flagged by sbt lintUnused

reason.text: Out of scope. These lintUnused warnings were already in build.sbt, and this change touches only test files under server/src/test. The task says not to edit build.sbt. The keys are Scala.js/webpack settings (stMinimize, webpackExtraArgs, webpackDevServerPort) that sbt commands or dev scripts may still read. Removing them or adding them to excludeLintKeys belongs in a separate build-cleanup change. The build and tests pass with these warnings.
